name: Basic Numerative Lexeme (0–99)

dimensions.form: Lexical unit (simple, derived, or compound); no internal syntax
dimensions.meaning: Specifies cardinality from zero to ninety-nine
dimensions.function: Can serve as factor or addition in complex numeratives
dimensions.distribution: Determiner, factor, addition; resists internal modification/coordination

1.definition: Lexical numeratives from zero to ninety-nine

constraints.description: Behaves as a lexical unit for syntax (no internal coordination or modification).

projection.target: Twenty-four can supply the single lexical unit that ordinal morphology targets in twenty-fourth. A construction such as three hundred twenty-four has additional phrasal structure, which is recoverable in reduced alternatives in an appropriate context.
projection.evidence: Reynolds combines prosody, ordinal morphology and ellipsis evidence for the lexical versus syntactic analysis.

curious.title: Number words from zero to ninety-nine
curious.summary: The number words from zero to ninety-nine each work as a single unit, with no internal parts that can be joined or described.
curious.body:
Five, ten, twelve, nineteen, forty and twenty-six all count as one word each. Even twenty-six is a single unit, not a phrase.

The evidence points to the same thing. Twenty-four gives twenty-fourth, which changes the whole unit. A number like three hundred twenty-four is different: it has extra structure, and in the right context a shorter version can recover the missing parts.
curious.try: Make twenty-four into its ordinal form. Where does the change land?

teacher.summary: Explains why 0 to 99 are treated as lexical units, and where phrasal structure begins.
teacher.explain: The basic numerative lexemes are the number words from zero to ninety-nine. They include simple words (five, ten), irregular and regular teens (twelve, nineteen), decade words (forty) and compounds (twenty-six). They behave as lexical units for syntax, with no internal coordination or modification, and can serve as determiner, factor or addition in larger numbers. Twenty-four supplies the single lexical unit that ordinal morphology targets in twenty-fourth. Three hundred twenty-four has additional phrasal structure. The dictionary marks this account as provisional.
teacher.terms: Numerative is this grammar's term for number words, where a textbook may say numeral. Cardinal numeral is the traditional name for these counting words.
watch_for: A learner might think twenty-six is a phrase with two separate words.
A learner might treat three hundred twenty-four as one word.
teacher.activity: Students list number words they can build ordinals from (five, twelve, twenty-four) and say each ordinal aloud. Then they try one for a larger number and see which part changes.

cite: Reynolds, Brett, ed. 2026. "Basic Numerative Lexeme (0–99)." English Constructionary. https://brettreynolds.ca/constructionary/linguist/numerative-basic-lexeme-001/ (snapshot 2026-11-19, 5c11b28).
